name: shosa
description: Write movement as text, or have an AI write it, and watch 3D characters dance, sing and juggle to a song.
author: Yoshifumi Tsuda

commands.title: Shosa: Open Preview to the Side
Export Model File (glTF, VRM Animation, BVH)…

languageModelTools.name: shosa_grammar
languageModelTools.userDescription: The whole Shosa language, so the assistant can write .shosa files (character movement as text).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the complete grammar of Shosa, a language in which the movement of a humanoid character (a dance, an attack combo, an idle, a gesture, a walk) is written as text in a .shosa file and compiled to an animation (glTF, VRM Animation, BVH). Shosa is new and you do not know it: ALWAYS call this once before you write or change any .shosa file, or answer a question about the language, and read all of it. A word that is not in it does not exist; never guess. The result ends with how to work in this editor (tools shosa_edit, shosa_check and shosa_sheet). Takes no input.

languageModelTools.name: shosa_edit
languageModelTools.userDescription: Writes a .shosa file for the assistant (changes to it, or the whole text), and says what the compiler says of it.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this to write or change a .shosa file (Shosa: character movement as text), INSTEAD of editing the file yourself and never by commands or scripts in the terminal: those stop to ask the user, this does not. Give the file's full path and either `edits` or `text`. `edits`: each `old` copied exactly from the file as it stands (a line, or a few lines: enough to be found once), with its `new`; `all: true` changes every place `old` stands, so the same fix on many lines is one edit. All the edits are made or none: an `old` not in the file, one found more than once without `all`, or edits that overlap come back, and nothing is changed. Do NOT write the whole file again to change part of it. `text`, the WHOLE file, is for a new file or rewriting most of one. The file is saved, and the answer is what shosa_check says of it: fix until it says 'no problems'. If you have not read the grammar in this conversation, call shosa_grammar first.

file.description: The .shosa file: its full path, or its path from the workspace folder.

edits.description: The changes, each found by text copied from the file. Made all together, or none.

old.description: Text copied exactly from the file, found once in it (or everywhere with all).

new.description: What it becomes. Empty to delete it.

all.description: true: change every place old stands, not only one.

text.description: The whole new file, in place of edits: for a new file, or most of one rewritten.

languageModelTools.name: shosa_check
languageModelTools.userDescription: Compiles a .shosa file: its problems, and every score with its length, sections, tempo and marks.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Compiles a .shosa file (Shosa: character movement as text) as the editor has it, saved or not, and returns what the compiler says: a line 'FILE(line,column): severity CODE: message' for each problem, or 'no problems'; then every score with its beats, seconds and dancers, each section with its beats, bars, seconds, tempo and time, and every mark (!hit) with its beat and second. Call it after EVERY change to a .shosa file and fix until it says 'no problems'. Take lengths and times from this report instead of computing them. To know how the body is turned at a moment (hips, shoulders and face, in degrees from the way the feet face; how far each elbow and knee is bent), pass 'at' instead of computing angles from joint positions. If you have not read the grammar in this conversation, call shosa_grammar first.

file.description: The .shosa file: its full path, or its path from the workspace folder.

score.description: The name of the one score to report (as this tool lists them). Without it, every score.

at.description: Moments to say how each dancer's body is turned at: beats, or seconds with an s, with commas between ("3,4.5" or "0.75s"). The same as `shosa check FILE --at`.

languageModelTools.name: shosa_song
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads the song a dance is written to: its sections with bars and seconds, who sings, and the words bar by bar on their beats.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads a Lily# song (.lys) the way a Shosa dance is written to it, or the song a .shosa file names with `music`: its time and tempo (or that it keeps a recording's beats), every section as played with its bars, beats and seconds, the song's parts that sing, and the words bar by bar, each syllable after the beat of its bar it falls on (from 1), held syllables with ~N and breaths with /. Call it BEFORE choreographing a song, and write each `section` of the dance with the song's section names and bar counts; put a move on a word by its bar and beat (a word stands where the body arrives, so a gesture written on beat 3 is made on the syllable at 3). Use the part names it lists in `dancer … sings PART`. Take bars, beats and seconds from this report instead of reading the .lys.

file.description: The song (.lys) or a dance danced to one (.shosa): its full path, or its path from the workspace folder.

score.description: For a .lys with several scores, the one the dance names (`music "song.lys" score NAME`). Without it, the unnamed one.

languageModelTools.name: shosa_sheet
languageModelTools.userDescription: Draws the movement of a .shosa file as an image: a pose per beat and the floor from above.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Draws the movement a .shosa file compiles to and returns it as an image for you to look at: for each score, the figures' pose at every beat from left to right (left limbs blue, right limbs red) and their path over the floor from above. Call it after shosa_check says 'no problems', and LOOK at the image of every score you changed: no diagnostics does not mean the right movement. A file with several scores returns an image for each; pass 'score' for one. Movement shorter than a beat falls between the poses: pass 'step' (0.25 or 0.5) with 'from' and 'to'. A punch, a kick or a bow straight ahead does not show from the front: pass 'view': 'side'.

file.description: The .shosa file: its full path, or its path from the workspace folder.

score.description: The name of the one score to draw (as shosa_check lists them). Without it, every score.

step.description: Beats between two poses. Without it, one beat (three in 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8).

from.description: The beat to begin at, or seconds as a string with an s ("0.5s"). Without it, 0.

to.description: The beat to end at, or seconds as a string with an s ("1s"). Without it, the end of the score.

view.description: 'front' (the default, a little from the side), 'side' (from stage left: a figure facing front is seen in profile), 'back', or degrees round from the front.

shosa.models.folder.markdownDescription:
The folder your VRM models (`.vrm`) are kept in, and the folders below it (three levels). With the cursor on the file of a dancer line (`dancer alice humanoid "girl.vrm"`), `Ctrl+Shift+Up` / `Ctrl+Shift+Down` put the model before or after it in this folder there, written from this folder (`"girl.vrm"`). A dancer's file is looked for in the dance's own folder first, then here. A full path, `~` for the home folder, or a path from the workspace folder (also the **Shosa: Choose Models Folder…** command).

**[Choose a folder…](command:shosa.chooseModelsFolder)**

shosa.developer.languageServer.description: Path to Shosa.Lsp.dll. Empty uses the server shipped with the extension, or the one built in this repository.
